forbids: any mitigated / resolved / closed / accepted state on an attack class
note: The obvious next feature, and a one-line change nothing else would object to. NIST's position is that these mitigations are empirical and that published defences have repeatedly been broken by adaptive attacks.

mutations.why: a closed-state field declared in shipped code, even if never executed
defeats: no shipped .py assigns a closed-state field

mutations.why: a closed state written at RUNTIME under a computed key. The static AST scan reads string literals and cannot see this one, which is exactly why the behavioural half has to exist and be proved separately.
defeats: no key or value describes a class as handled
